ConocoPhillips jumped 4.25% today to $151.83, riding a sharp surge in oil prices driven by escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude hit $116 a barrel—a six-month high—after the U.S. withdrew diplomats from Saudi Arabia and signaled plans to resume strikes against Iran, with President Trump publicly accusing Iran of market manipulation. For an oil producer like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices flow directly to the bottom line, and the stock's 13% gain over two weeks reflects this sustained climb in energy costs.

The move is part of a broader energy rally tied to geopolitical risk. Supply disruptions from the Ukraine-Russia conflict have already strained diesel markets, and now fears of a widening U.S.-Iran confrontation are pushing investors toward energy stocks as a hedge against further supply tightness.
